methodology: Verse-by-verse first-pass screening against Quran Arabic and Yusuf Ali translation; earlier English primary translations inspected for Exodus and Deuteronomy, other source locators remain pending direct primary inspection. All candidates hidden pending original-language, edition, dating and manuscript checks; no borrowing claims.

verses.assessment: Single origin and mate: compare Genesis 2:21–24, but Qur'an does not name Adam/Eve in this verse or describe rib surgery.
Orphan property stewardship: compare Exodus 22:22–24 on protection of the fatherless; it does not prescribe the Qur'anic asset-transfer rule.
Orphans, marriage and justice among wives: no specific earlier textual equivalence established; do not reduce verse to generic polygyny motif.
Bridal gifts: possible ancient marriage-gift practices require precise documentary evidence; none verified.
Entrusted property and support for dependents: no source-specific earlier parallel established.
Orphan guardianship and property handover on maturity: compare biblical concern for orphans, but no equivalent age/test/accounting rule established.
Inheritance shares for women and men: stage Numbers 27:8–11 as a legal contrast, not identical inheritance distribution.
Provision for non-heir relatives and poor during division: no precise earlier source established.
Concern for vulnerable descendants: broad moral motif only.
Punishment for consuming orphan wealth: compare Exodus 22:22–24 as an ethical/theological parallel; punishment imagery differs.

staged_candidates.caveat: Genesis specifies a side/rib and woman formed from man; Qur'an 4:1 says a single soul and its mate, without that physical detail
Exodus forbids mistreatment and threatens judgment, not a detailed fiduciary regime or ingestion-of-fire imagery
Numbers provides daughters inheritance when no son, while Qur'an 4:7 explicitly grants women shares; allocation differs
Deuteronomy protects fatherless justice and harvest access, not Qur'anic guardianship accounting
